title: Astrid and the Undertow
premise: After her mother's funeral, Petra Thornbury returns to the coastal town of Wrenlow to catalog a house full of silence — and discovers that Halvorsen House, where she spent one transformative childhood summer, is being auctioned to settle debts she never knew existed. Among the bidders is Elias Vane, the boy who once saved her from the undertow and then vanished from her life, now a wealthy developer intent on demolishing the house. As the auction date closes in, Petra must excavate what really happened that summer — why her mother never spoke of it, why Elias was sent away, and what price each of them paid for surviving. In the end, Petra outbids no one but herself: she lets the house go, speaks her goodbye aloud on its empty lawn, and offers Elias not forgiveness but truth, choosing at last to belong to her own life rather than her mother's silence.
about_author: Xanthe Eastwick is a former estate appraiser who spent a decade inventorying other people's inheritances before turning to fiction. She writes from a rented cottage on the North Sea coast, where she has never learned to swim.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Three days after the funeral, she receives condolences with practiced grace while packing her mother's untouched kitchen. A solicitor's letter arrives: Halvorsen House, the summer home she thought long sold, is entering auction. Beat: grief met by avoidance; the first crack in her armor.

chapters.title: Inventory of Silence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She catalogs her mother's belongings for the estate sale, finding drawers of unopened letters and a photograph of two children on a beach she doesn't remember visiting. Her brother Marcus urges her to sign the auction paperwork quickly. Beat: unease beneath competence.

chapters.title: Wrenlow, Off Season
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She drives to the coastal town against Marcus's advice, finding Halvorsen House shuttered and tagged for auction. The town remembers her; she remembers nothing clearly. An old neighbor, Mrs. Adeyemi, calls her by a childhood nickname. Beat: the past asserting itself.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Pulled
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with a flashback. A memory surfaces: drowning in the undertow at nine years old, and a boy named Elias dragging her ashore, both of them sworn to secrecy. She wakes on Mrs. Adeyemi's sofa, disoriented. Beat: the buried breaking through.

chapters.title: Lot Forty-Seven
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the auction preview she encounters Elias Vane — grown, polished, bidding aggressively on the property. He pretends not to know her. His firm plans a resort on the site. Beat: recognition denied; antagonism established.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Searching the house attic, she finds her mother's journal, its final third pages torn out, and a deed showing the house was never sold — only hidden. Marcus phones, angry she's digging. Beat: suspicion turns toward family.

chapters.title: Elias, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. We see his side: the summer he was sent away after the drowning, the father who used the rescue as leverage, the empire built on never looking back. He tells himself the demolition is just business. Beat: antagonist humanized; his own silence revealed.

chapters.title: The Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Mrs. Adeyemi reveals fragments: after the drowning, Petra's mother blamed Elias's family, and the two households warred until the boy was removed from town. Petra realizes her mother tore out the account of that summer deliberately. Beat: betrayal sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Auction Terms
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The solicitor explains the reserve price and a strange codicil: the seller — her mother — stipulated that any buyer must preserve the boathouse. Elias's lawyers are contesting it. Petra realizes her mother left a message. Beat: hope kindled.

chapters.title: Undertow, Again
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Under pressure from investors, Elias visits the boathouse alone and finds carved initials — his and Petra's — inside the door. He pockets the old brass key he'd kept twenty-five years. Beat: the past cornering him despite himself.

chapters.title: Marcus's Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Confronting Marcus, she learns he has known about the auction for months and quietly arranged financing through Elias's firm — trading the house's fate for his own solvency. Beat: the second betrayal; family as transaction.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Key
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Breaking into the boathouse, she finds a tin box her mother hid: the torn journal pages, describing not blame but guilt — her mother had been on the beach that day and froze while a child pulled Petra out. Beat: the central secret surfaced.

chapters.title: Frozen
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, flashback-heavy. The full account: her mother watched her daughter drown and could not move; Elias, ten years old, acted instead. Her mother's lifelong silence was shame, not protection. Petra grieves the mother she invented. Beat: devastation and clarity.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. His investors threaten to pull funding unless the codicil falls. Elias, holding the key and the memory of initials, wavers — then doubles down publicly, cold in an interview about 'progress.' Beat: the corruption of power tightening its grip.

chapters.title: Confrontation at High Tide
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She confronts Elias on the seawall, offering him the torn pages. He refuses to read them, insisting the past is 'settled accounts.' She sees the boy who saved her has become a man who cannot be saved by anyone. Beat: rising conflict; empathy curdling.

chapters.title: The Reserve Is Met
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Auction day approaches; a rival bidder, a preservation trust with thin funds, asks Petra to speak for the house. Marcus demands she stop sabotaging him. Petra must choose between the house, her brother, and her own voice. Beat: stakes converge.

chapters.title: Bidding War
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the auction, the trust and Elias's firm escalate bids beyond reason. When the trust falters, Petra stands and reads aloud — not a bid, but the first page of her mother's confession, in front of the whole town and press. Beat: climax begins; silence broken publicly.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The room goes still. She finishes the reading, then says her goodbye to the house directly — naming her mother's failure and her love in the same breath. Elias walks out mid-sentence. The gavel falls to the trust at a price no one expected. Beat: emotional climax; the goodbye completed.

chapters.title: What the Money Buys
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Defeated and exposed, Elias sits in his car outside the sold house all night. He finally reads the pages Petra left on his windshield. Beat: the antagonist's reckoning; power shown as poverty.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She and Elias meet once more on the empty beach. No reconciliation — she declines his apology and his offer of restitution — but they bury the tin box together below the tideline, each keeping half the key. Beat: honest ending over false repair.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Back home, she signs the final estate papers without the practiced smile, telling Marcus plainly what she knows and what she will no longer carry. The preservation trust invites her to advise on the boathouse memorial. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Undertow Lets Go
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, epilogue. A year later, she stands at the restored boathouse as children swim under supervision, and she swims — badly, bravely — for the first time since age nine. She writes the last line of her own account. Beat: survival's true price paid; release.
